ca_butt_rock_outcrop.blurb: Butt Rock Outcrop stands on the northern flank of the San Bernardino Mountains, in the Juniper Flats foothills southeast of Apple Valley, at roughly 5,500 feet. It is a small crag with nine routes: four sport lines, four trad lines and one top rope. Grades start at 5.10 and climb into the 5.13s, with the bulk in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits climbers who already lead hard rather than beginners. Two sharp arêtes stand out among the lines, and the rest of the wall adds a handful of varied routes. As the high point of the surrounding area, it is a short outing for a few focused burns rather than a full-day venue.

ca_beach_right_side_the.blurb: The right side of the Beach is a cliff at Whitney Portal, above Lone Pine on the eastern flank of the Sierra, at about 8,400 feet. It has nine routes, eight of them trad and one sport, all between 5.11 and 5.12. The wall is longer, steeper and more sustained than its left-hand neighbour, with climbing on small knobs, edges and pimples; the bolts are not spaced at every body length, so expect to place gear and commit. Trees shade the base, which is a flat spot that makes a comfortable place to hang between tries. One 70 m rope handles every line here.

ca_cove_the_3.blurb: The Cove is a small crag in the Downtown section of Margheritaville, in the high desert of the Apple Valley area, at about 3,600 feet. Its outcrops run along a dirt road, starting with a short tower beside the road and continuing up to a deeper recess where the taller lines are. Nine routes, mostly sport with two trad lines, span roughly 5.8 to 5.11, and most fall in the 5.9 to 5.10 band, which makes it a fair stop for a mid-grade leader. The walls face southeast, so it works as a place to climb on cold days.

ca_circle_crack_boulders.blurb: Circle Crack Boulders is a cluster of problems on Mount Rubidoux, the boulder-covered hill above Riverside, at about 900 feet in the Inland Empire. It has nine problems spanning a wide range: a couple of very easy ones, a handful around V4 and V5, and three much harder lines near V8. The cluster is built around the Circle Crack feature and its neighbouring arête, and two caves at the site give a place to wait out the heat. The setting is a city park, so expect company and bring a bag to carry out any trash.

ca_alcove_the.blurb: The Alcove is a bouldering wall on the Sherwin Plateau near Mammoth Lakes, in the Eastern Sierra, at about 7,100 feet. The main feature is a wave of rock that is vertical low down and overhangs near the top, with large, sharp pockets for holds. Nine problems cover V0 up to V5, most of them in the V0 to V3 range, with a girdle traverse and a harder direct line at the upper end. It is an easy place to warm up or to bring mixed company, and the landings below the wall are flat. A faint path along a sandy wash leads in from the parking area.

ca_uphill_boulder_2.blurb: The Uphill boulder is a pair of boulders in the Muffins group at Castle Rock State Park, in the Santa Cruz Mountains of the South Bay, at about 2,850 feet. They sit about a hundred feet above the Middle Muffin, trending slightly left. Problems here run from the lower grades up to around V4, with the larger share at the easy end, so it fits a short session at the Muffins rather than a destination of its own. The sandstone around Castle Rock is brittle and breaks easily when damp.

ca_1st_section.blurb: The 1st Section is the far left end of the LTA cliff band beside the Sonora Pass Highway, at about 7,200 feet. It has nine routes, mostly top-rope and trad, with a single sport line. Grades run from 5.4 up to 5.10, with the larger share in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, so beginners and intermediate climbers both have something to work on. Each line is marked at its base with a painted letter or number, which makes it easy to match what you are climbing to a route. The cliff band continues to the right, and the route labelled A is the left-most line.

ca_beetle_buttress.blurb: Beetle Buttress is a small formation in Joshua Tree National Park, in the Cockroach Crag section of the Lost Horse Area, at about 4,300 feet. It leans against a hillside and holds nine routes, eight trad and one top rope. Grades start around 5.4 and reach 5.11, with a cluster at 5.10, so it offers a few easy leads as well as harder crack and corner lines. The routes are short, and the stone is in good condition. It pairs well with nearby formations for a day of cragging.

_conflicts.ca_uphill_boulder_2: Stored count is 9 problems; the area page https://www.mountainproject.com/area/118208775/uphill-boulder lists one (V4), and the parent https://www.mountainproject.com/area/120021423/muffins-and-waterfall-boulders lists one.
